feed.title: NPR Topics: National
feed.subtitle: NPR coverage of national news, U.S. politics, elections, business, arts, culture, health and science, and technology. Subscribe to the NPR Nation RSS feed.

entry.title: Arizona's taps won't run dry, but water bills will go up under federal plan for Colorado River
entry.summary: New federal rules mean Arizona will be getting a lot less water from the Colorado river. City leaders say they've been planning for years and no one will run out, but keeping taps flowing is expensive.

entry.title: The Nancy Grace Roman Telescope begins its journey into deep space
entry.summary: NASA launched a telescope named after Nancy Grace Roman, the pioneering astronomer whose work helped make Hubble and generations of space telescopes possible.

entry.title: Finally, an economic indicator you can eat
entry.summary: A corn dog may look like lunch. But to an economist, the price is a bigger story about food prices and inflation.

entry.title: Insanity defenses rarely work. Lindsay Clancy's case may be different
entry.summary: Insanity defenses are notoriously difficult to win. But Massachusetts law could give Lindsay Clancy a better chance.

entry.title: He offered strangers $10 to tie his shoe. Then things got weird
entry.summary: Would $10 convince you to walk up to a stranger and tie their shoe? One Minneapolis artist turned that question into delightfully public chaos.

entry.title: Haitians in Springfield, Ohio, avoid leaving home as ICE activity intensifies
entry.summary: As threats of deportation loom, some Haitians in Springfield, Ohio, are hiding in their homes, too afraid to visit their churches.

entry.title: More school districts are shrinking. New research asks whether closures work
entry.summary: School districts across the country are closing campuses as enrollment falls. New research says the financial savings may be smaller than expected.

entry.title: What to know about FAA moves to fire two controllers after deadly LaGuardia crash
entry.summary: The FAA's response to a deadly crash is opening a larger debate about staffing, safety and a workplace practice controllers call the "early shove."

entry.title: ICE arrests are surging as the administration targets more immigrants
entry.summary: ICE made nearly 50,000 arrests in July -- the highest monthly total of Trump's second term -- as enforcement expands to more places like airports, courthouses and immigration check-ins.

entry.title: Who gets to be Mary Todd Lincoln next? There's a list
entry.summary: Oh, Mary! has discovered an unusual way to keep a Broadway hit fresh: keep replacing Mary Todd Lincoln with someone completely different.
